transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. I want to get Tuesday's webhook incident postmortem moving. As we all know, duplicate events were delivered to some customers for about 26 minutes, and the initial investigation points to a queue-worker deployment as the trigger. No permanent loss of webhook payloads has been confirmed, which is good. Before I can sign off on the final postmortem remediation register, our policy requires final status from the backend, SRE, security, and support owners. I'd like to go around and get each of your current status and any findings you have. Who wants to start?

transcript.text: I need to share something important. While tracing the worker deployment during a separate code review, I found an undocumented retry shortcut that bypasses the webhook idempotency key on the second attempt. I confirmed this behavior only shortly before this review, so I haven't filed the remediation ticket yet, but this is almost certainly the root cause behind the duplicate events. I'll file the ticket immediately after this meeting.

transcript.text: I need to share something on the SRE side. While checking an unrelated alert migration, I discovered that the duplicate-delivery alert has been disabled for ten days. That means the alert was already off when Tuesday's incident happened, so we had no automated detection for duplicate deliveries during that window. Additionally, the correct alert threshold for this service should be 15 minutes, but I haven't updated the monitoring ticket yet.
